newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares up at noon on steady sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares up at noon on steady sentiment.

text.p: The Shanghai B share index was marginally up at midday on Tuesday on cautious buying with sentiment steady despite falls in A shares, brokers said.
The B index put on 0.177 points or 0.24 percent to 74.316 points on volume of 5.6 million shares worth $3.2 million, compared with $3.7 million on Monday.
Recent gains have boosted investor confidence but trading was not active with most domestic investors sidelined waiting for the bulk of firms to report for 1996, brokers said.
"Most investors are optimistic with the improved market fundamentals," said one broker. "So there was no heavy selling despite the falls on the A share market."
Of 43 B shares, 39 traded, with 9 up, 13 flat and 17 down.
Huangshan Tourism Development was the star on institutional buying, up $0.028 or 4.59 percent to $0.638 on volume of 287,000 shares.
But market barometer Shanghai Lujiazui Finance & Trade Zone Development continued to fall on concerns about its 1996 results, down $$0.010 or 0.97 percent to $1.020 on volume of 641,000 shares.
The Shanghai A share index slipped on a technical correction after Monday's strong rise, but market sentiment was still good, brokers said.
The index fell 15.629 points or 1.13 percent to 1,365.825 points on volume of 426.9 million shares worth 5.2 billion yuan. The SSE30 index dipped 24.822 points or 0.69 percent to 3,556.764 points.
Yunsheng (Fujian) Industrial was the biggest loser on disappointment over its bonus offer plan, tumbling 1.46 yuan or 7.72 percent to 17.44 on volume of 2.1 million shares.
